Skip to content ⌘ Ctrl k Knowledge Base Website Changelog Book a Demo Login More Getting Started Introduction Quick Start Setup Channel Configuration User Guide Pylonboarding Agents Assist Agent Automations Slack Agent Skills Connectors User Memories Support Agent Support Workflows Omnichannel Support Issues SLAs and Timers Support Hours CSAT Ticket Forms Assignment Rules Email Phone Support User QA Platform Custom Fields Tags Taxonomy Teams Triggers Macros Command Search Roles & User Management Resources AI Reports Surveys Audit Logs Languages & Localization Custom Objects Knowledge Base Overview Articles & Collections Translations Missing Content Analytics Styling & Customization Custom Authentication Search Redirects SEO & AI Crawlers Customer Portal Overview Styling & Customization Portal Experience Access Control Custom Authentication Chat Widget Overview Styling Functionality Chat Experience Chat Setup Custom Domain Identity Verification JavaScript API Mobile SDKs Account Intelligence Customer Overview Accounts Opportunities Notebooks Tasks & Projects Activities Fields Product Intelligence Feature Requests Closing the Loop Reporting & Analytics Analytics Default Dashboards Custom Dashboards Broadcasts Overview Create a Broadcast Analytics Integrations CRM Ticketing Alerting Chat Incident Management Call Recording Calendar Data Warehouse Codebase Pylon MCP Security Security Overview IP Addresses Developer API Authentication API conventions Errors Rate limits API reference External IDs SDKs CLI Custom Apps Embedded Iframes Webhooks Powered by GitBook On this page Copy On this page Developer API Authentication How to authenticate with Pylon's API The Pylon API uses Bearer authentication. This means you’ll need to pass your API token in the header of your request: Copy Authorization: Bearer <token> Generate an API token in the Pylon dashboard . API regions Pylon’s API is available in two regions. Use the base URL that matches where your Pylon tenant is hosted: US region: https://api.usepylon.com EU region: https://api.eu.usepylon.com Both regions use the same API endpoints and authentication. Configure your integration to use the region where your Pylon tenant is hosted. You can tell a token's region from its prefix: Prefix Region pylon_api_eu_ EU pylon_api_ US Tokens created before prefixes were introduced have no prefix. Sending a token to the other region's API returns 401 with the wrong_region_token error code, and the message names the correct URL. Once you've created a token, call the /me endpoint to retrieve details about your organization and confirm your token works. Create an API token Only Admins can create and manage API tokens. Go to Settings > Integrations & dev > API . On the Tokens tab, click Create API Token . Enter a Name . Choose who the token acts as: Leave Act as user or bot (optional) empty to give the token its own identity. Pick a Role to control what it can access, and optionally upload an icon. Or select a teammate or bot. The token uses that user's current role and permissions. Optionally, add an IP allowlist (see below). Click Create and copy the token. Pylon shows it only once. Tokens don't expire, and their access is controlled only by the role. There are no separate scopes. Roles A token with its own identity uses the role you pick when you create it. You can change the role later with Edit . Older tokens that have no role act as Admin. A token that acts as a user or bot has no role of its own. It always uses that user's current role, so changing the user's role changes what the token can do. See Roles and user management for what each role allows. Who actions are attributed to Token with its own identity: actions show up under the token's name and icon. Token that acts as a user or bot: actions are attributed to that user or bot. Bots Bots are identities for automation, so API activity is attributed to the bot instead of to a teammate. Bots can't sign in to Pylon. To create one, go to Settings > Workspace > Users , open the Bots tab, and click New Bot . Give it a name, an avatar, and a role. Then select the bot under Act as user or bot when you create a token. IP allowlist Add IP addresses (for example 203.0.113.10 ) or CIDR blocks (for example 203.0.113.0/24 ) to restrict where the token can be used. You can add up to 20 entries. If the list is empty, the token works from any IP. Pylon checks the public IP address your requests come from, so add the public egress IPs or ranges of the servers that call the API. Private addresses such as 10.0.0.0/8 or 192.168.0.0/16 never match. A request from an address that isn't on the list returns 401 with the invalid_api_token error code. Manage tokens The Tokens tab shows each token's Acts as , Token preview , Role , Created by , Last used , and Created values. From the … menu on a token you can: Edit: change the name, role, or IP allowlist. Duplicate Token: create a new token with the same settings. Rotate: generate a new token value. The current token stops working immediately. Delete: permanently revoke the token. Calls using it stop working immediately. View Activity: open the token's request logs. Review API request logs Only Admins can view request logs. Go to Settings > Integrations & dev > API and open the Logs tab, or choose View Activity from a token's … menu to see only that token's requests. Filter by token, or choose All tokens , and by a date range of up to 90 days. The range defaults to the last 7 days. Each request shows when it was made, the token, who it acted as, the method, endpoint, response status, source IP, user agent, and request ID. Requests made with a token that was since deleted still appear. Requests rejected for authentication or rate limits aren't logged, and older requests may not show a token. When tokens are revoked automatically When a user is deactivated, Pylon deletes: every API token that user created, and every API token that acts as that user. Before you deactivate someone who created tokens your integrations rely on, create replacement tokens from another Admin's account. An Admin who has created Admin-role tokens can't be moved to a different role until those tokens are deleted. Previous API Next API conventions Last updated 26 days ago Was this helpful? pages.text: Channel Configuration | Pylon For the complete documentation index, see llms.txt . Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending .md to page URLs. Skip to content ⌘ Ctrl k Knowledge Base Website Changelog Book a Demo Login More Getting Started Introduction Quick Start Setup Channel Configuration User Guide Pylonboarding Agents Assist Agent Automations Slack Agent Skills Connectors User Memories Support Agent Support Workflows Omnichannel Support Issues SLAs and Timers Support Hours CSAT Ticket Forms Assignment Rules Email Phone Support User QA Platform Custom Fields Tags Taxonomy Teams Triggers Macros Command Search Roles & User Management Resources AI Reports Surveys Audit Logs Languages & Localization Custom Objects Knowledge Base Overview Articles & Collections Translations Missing Content Analytics Styling & Customization Custom Authentication Search Redirects SEO & AI Crawlers Customer Portal Overview Styling & Customization Portal Experience Access Control Custom Authentication Chat Widget Overview Styling Functionality Chat Experience Chat Setup Custom Domain Identity Verification JavaScript API Mobile SDKs Account Intelligence Customer Overview Accounts Opportunities Notebooks Tasks & Projects Activities Fields Product Intelligence Feature Requests Closing the Loop Reporting & Analytics Analytics Default Dashboards Custom Dashboards Broadcasts Overview Create a Broadcast Analytics Integrations CRM Ticketing Alerting Chat Incident Management Call Recording Calendar Data Warehouse Codebase Pylon MCP Security Security Overview IP Addresses Developer API Custom Apps Embedded Iframes Webhooks Powered by GitBook On this page Copy On this page Getting Started Channel Configuration To integrate Pylon seamlessly with Slack, there's two main steps to configuration: setting up your Internal Threads workflow, and then actually connecting individual channels in Pylon. Step 1: Setting up Internal Threads Internal threads are a dedicated threads in Slack to discuss and collaborate on new customer issues internally. All discussion in these threads will be synced back to Pylon! We recommend setting this up prior to connecting any other channels so they'll be ready to sync as soon as you pull data into Pylon. For Small Teams Make one public channel called #customer-alerts . For Larger Teams If you have multiple team members handling accounts, we recommend opening up one channel per person on your team that's responsible for handling account messages. For example, if you have three CSMs Alex, Sabrina, and John: #alex-customers #sabrina-customers #john-customers If you’re in a public workspace, or just want to make your internal threads in a private channel, add Pylon to the channel following the below instructions, but choose Triage Channel . Go to Settings > Internal Threads (under Workflows) and select the first template. Under "Send To", pick the channel(s) you created above! You can always change where internal threads are created, or segment issues by account owner or other properties to create internal threads in different places for more complex team structures. Step 2: Enabling Channels Channels in Pylon are bucketed into three categories: Customer Channels, where you're talking directly with your customers Community Channels, which typically contain users from many different companies Internal Channels, where users within your company are asking questions to other team members Each type of channel can be enabled in a slightly different way. Enable a Customer Channel Pylon can be enabled in customer channels by one of 3 methods: Bulk updating via the Accounts dashboard in Pylon Manual enablement directly from a Slack channel Autolinking via standard naming conventions Private customer channels must be enabled directly in Slack. Accounts Dashboard Select "Accounts" in the sidebar, and then click the purple "Add Account" button in the top right of the screen (which should bring you to the menu below). Pick "Slack" to bulk enable Pylon in relevant customer channels. Slack Pylon will have function in customer channels that you explicitly enable it in. If you want it to be enabled in channels automatically, you can use our CRM widget to create and setup channels automatically. Go to your customer channel Type /invite @Pylon (or whatever you set as the Pylon bot display name ) and press enter. You’ll get a prompt to enable Pylon in the channel. Select Customer Channel . Fill out the modal with your preferences, including selecting the desired triage channel (these will be saved for the next time) Autolink Channels If you have a common pattern to your slack channels (i.e. putting ext- at the beginning of all external channels), you can autolink them with Pylon. Head over to the Account Configuration page and find the 'External Slack channel linking' section. You'll be able to configure the pattern of your Slack channels there so they will sync automatically moving forward. Microsoft Teams has a separate automatic linking configuration for new standard and shared channels. See Microsoft Teams for eligibility and account-matching rules. Enable a Community Channel A community channel is a channel with users from many different companies, typically in a community workspace. Link this channel the same way you would a customer channel, but choose Community Channel once inviting Pylon to the channel. Enable an Internal Channel An internal channel is a channel where users from within your company are asking questions, typically to the support or customer-facing team. You should link these types of channels only from the Pylon dashboard. You can see here how to do this. Previous Setup Next User Guide Last updated 26 days ago Was this helpful? Pylon is a pretty powerful platform with lots of customization to make your day-to-day productive and fun. Here are some of the things you'll want to get setup or learn about to help you get the most value out of Pylon. Keyboard Shortcuts All keyboard shortcuts can be found in-app by choosing "Keyboard Shortcuts" from your profile menu at the bottom left corner of the screen. General Navigation To quickly navigate around Pylon, view recently visited pages, or search for specific customer issues, knowledge base articles, accounts, etc use Command Search by hitting Cmd-K or Ctrl-K from anywhere in Pylon. Managing Issues Issue keyboard shortcuts are available when you are viewing an issue. Shortcut Action j and k Navigate between issues s Change the status of an issue z Snooze an issue a Assign an issue f Toggle fullscreen mode m Run a Macro Esc Exit out of an issue Cmd-j AI Copilot Cmd-Enter or Ctrl-Enter Send a message Cmd-Shift-Enter or Ctrl-Shift-Enter Send a message and close the issue Cmd-Option-Enter or Ctrl-Option-Enter Send a message, close the issue, and move to the next issue Dark Mode Toggle dark mode from your Profile page in Settings or by typing Cmd-k and then Dark Mode . Notification Preferences Under the Notifications page, customize which notifications you'd like to receive and where you'd like to receive them. You can also access them from both the profile and settings menus in the bottom left corner of your screen. Notifications are grouped into tabs: Issues , Projects & tasks , Knowledge base , Feature management , and Connectors & tools . For each event, choose whether to be notified In-app , in Slack , with a Desktop notification, or by Email . Turn on Enable Sound to play a sound for in-app notifications. Issue notifications you can configure: I'm assigned an issue by a teammate I'm assigned an issue by triggers or assignment rules I'm mentioned in an internal note New customer message on an issue I follow New message from your team on an issue I follow Issue that I follow is unsnoozed Issue that I'm assigned to breached SLA Email notifications about issue messages include the message text, up to 5,000 characters. Longer messages are cut off with an ellipsis; open the link in the email to read the full message in Pylon. In-app notifications will show up under your notifications tray, accessible via. the Bell icon on the top left. The tray has All , Unread , and Mentions tabs, and a Mark all read button. If Desktop notifications are on but you aren't seeing them, check that your browser allows notifications from Pylon. Signatures If you'll be sending emails from Pylon, consider setting up an email signature on your Profile page. The signature will get automatically appended in the editor when you're replying to emails. Previous Channel Configuration Next Pylonboarding Last updated 26 days ago Was this helpful?
